A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same REArtGS work and support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; supplementary materials mentioned in the text are not included in either supplied file.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.5 report original reconstruction and generation experiments on PartNet-Mobility and AKB-48, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative outputs and ablations.

after.justification: The original empirical evaluations remain, with additional ArtGS comparisons, Eyeglasses results and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same SDF-guided Gaussian reconstruction, motion-constrained deformation, dynamic-part segmentation, optimization objectives and textured-mesh extraction. The added baseline does not change REArtGS.

E1.justification: Table 5 and Figure 6 add Eyeglasses to the real-world evaluation, expanding reported AKB-48 coverage from five to six categories. The synthetic categories and reconstruction/generation tasks remain unchanged. Drawer was already evaluated in v1 despite its newly added illustration.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 5 add ArtGS without depth supervision across the main synthetic and real-world reconstruction/generation comparisons, substantially broadening comparison against a directly relevant articulated-object Gaussian-splatting method. Figure 4 replaces A-SDF with ArtGS in the qualitative comparison; A-SDF remains in the quantitative tables.

E3.justification: The newly added ArtGS comparisons explicitly disable depth supervision for input comparability. Section 4.1 otherwise retains the same view sampling, input counts and metrics. No changed protocol is documented for the revised Foldchair scores.

E4.justification: The SDF/unbiased-regularization ablation in Table 3 and motion-constraint ablation in Table 4 retain their settings and results. Additional qualitative benchmark outputs do not introduce a new robustness test or analytical question.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores and category averages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional results use the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main tables gain ArtGS results, and Table 5 gains Eyeglasses results and aggregates over six categories. Table 2 changes REArtGS Foldchair CD(ws) from 13.55 to 0.41 and F1 from 0.248 to 0.465, changing the corresponding means from 5.41 to 4.10 and 0.276 to 0.298. Figure 6 adds Drawer and Eyeglasses outputs. These substantially expand comparative evidence, but the numerical revisions are unexplained and Table 4 retains the old means.

T1.justification: The supplied mathematical content, including Equations 1–17, SDF definitions, motion assumptions and parameterizations, is unchanged. Neither PDF includes the separately referenced supplementary proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: textured reconstruction and unseen-state generation from two states using geometric and motion constraints. Claims of superior synthetic and real-world performance remain unchanged in meaning.

C2.justification: Explanations involving geometric initialization, opacity regularization and constrained deformation remain unchanged. Both conclusions identify the same limitations concerning camera-pose priors and transparent materials.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project website and changes the code-release promise from within four months to after acceptance; neither establishes that code has been released. New table captions disclose ArtGS's omitted depth supervision. Existing implementation and hardware descriptions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the ArtGS paper, Building Interactable Replicas of Complex Articulated Objects via Gaussian Splatting, as reference 18 and cites it in comparisons. The related-work discussion and existing research positioning are otherwise unchanged; subsequent reference-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: Language changes are limited mainly to the abstract's code/website sentence and added comparison-caption explanations. Section order and almost all scientific prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 replaces and rearranges comparator columns, and Figure 6 expands from three to five object examples. Tables 1, 2 and 5 gain comparison rows; Table 5 also gains Eyeglasses and moves from page 8 to page 9. The overall display organization and two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: The ArtGS comparisons and additional real-world evidence strengthen evaluation, but v3 introduces unresolved reporting inconsistencies. Tables 2 and 4 agree on generation means in v1 but disagree in v3, and Section 4.1 still states five real-world categories despite six in Table 5. That table also reports PARIS reconstruction CD(rs) mean 1.336 although its listed category values average approximately 1.596. The useful additions and reduced numerical consistency prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
